content.title: Oscars 2026: How to Watch All the Oscar-Nominated Documentaries and Which Will Win
content.text: Skip to main contentMenuMenuOSCARS 2026From prison reform in the South to the indoctrination of Russian children living during the invasion of Ukraine, all about the nominated docs at the Oscars 2026.March 11, 2026Andrea Gibson and their wife Megan Falley, the couple at the center of Oscar-nominated documentary Come See Me in the Good Light.The common thread that binds all of the nominated documentaries at Oscars 2026: small acts of bravery with the potential for a big impact. Sara Shahverdi, the first female councilor in her Iranian village, fights for progress against patriarchy in Cutting Through Rocks. Russian school teacher Pavel “Pasha” Talankin documents educational indoctrination during the invasion of Ukraine in Mr. Nobody Against Putin. Incarcerated men expose their prisons’ brutal living conditions via contraband cellphones in The Alabama Solution. Colorado’s former poet laureate Andrea Gibson confronts the final stretch of their four-year cancer battle with wife Megan Falley in Come See Me in the Good Light. And in The Perfect Neighbor, a tight-knit community rallies around a grieving family—and against a local lone wolf with a gun.Keep ReadingContinue reading with a Vanity Fair subscription and get unlimited access, exclusive newsletters, and more.
